# @llazyemail/template-runtime-display API

Package: `@llazyemail/template-runtime-display`.
Node 24+. Named exports only. No default export. No runtime dependencies. No template registry.
Import the package root. Builds: ESM `dist/index.js`, CJS `dist/index.cjs`, browser IIFE `dist/index.global.js` (global `TemplateRuntimeDisplay`), types `dist/index.d.ts`.

The runtime is synchronous and stateless. Callers own templates. The same template, props, and slots return the same HTML, including whitespace. Trace `ms` may differ. Omitted optional strings become `''`. Rendered HTML does not contain the word `undefined`. Prop values and slot strings are concatenated as HTML with no escape step.

## Model

`Template<TProps>`:

- `id: string` — non-empty. Shown on errors and in `explain`.
- `parts` — ordered `{ id, render }`. `render(ctx) => string`.
- `compose(parts, ctx) => string` — stitches the part record into the final document.

`RenderContext<TProps>`:

- `templateId`
- `props` — the same object the caller passed, not a copy
- `slots` — frozen shallow copy of the caller's slots

`defineTemplate(template)` validates, copies each part (`id` and `render`), freezes the part list and the template, and returns that copy. Mutating the input array later does not change the defined template.

Validation throws `RenderError` (`partId` is `template`, `trace` is empty) when:

- the template id is empty
- a part id is empty
- a part id is `compose` (reserved)
- a part id is duplicated
- `compose` is not a function

`renderTemplate` runs the same checks.

Part ids are the debug names. Put each piece of custom code in its own part.

## renderTemplate(template, props, options?): RenderResult

`options.onError` is `'throw'` (default) or `'collect'`. `options.slots` is optional.

Each part runs in order. The return value passes through these rules:

- `string` — stored. Status `ok`, or `empty` when the string is `''`.
- `null` or `undefined` — stored as `''`, status `empty`.
- any other value — `TypeError`, status `error`.
- a throw — status `error`. `Error` instances keep `name` and `message`. Anything else becomes `{ name: 'Error', message: String(value) }`.

`throw`: the broken part is recorded, later parts are `skipped` and do not run, and `RenderError` is thrown. `message` is `template "<id>" failed at part "<partId>": <message>`. `cause` is the original throw.

`collect`: the broken part is stored as `''`, later parts run, and the returned `RenderResult.ok` is false.

Compose then receives `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` of the stored HTML (missing parts are absent only if compose is called by hand) and the same context. A non-string return is a `TypeError`. A compose throw uses part id `compose`. In `collect`, `html` is `''`, `ok` is false, and `composeError` is set. In `throw`, `RenderError.partId` is `compose`.

`RenderResult`:

- `templateId`, `ok`, `html`
- `parts`: frozen `PartTrace[]` (`id`, `status`, `html`, `chars`, `ms`, optional `error: { name, message }`)
- `composeError` optional, only for a collected compose failure

`status` is `ok | empty | error | skipped`.

## explain(result | RenderError): string

One text block for logs. A `RenderError` prints `error.message` (it contains `failed at part`). A `RenderResult` prints `<templateId>: ok|failed (<n> parts, <n> chars)`. Then one line per part: `<id> <status> <chars> chars <ms>ms` plus ` <name>: <message>` when that part has an error. A collected compose failure adds `compose error <name>: <message>`. Part HTML is not inlined. Read `parts[].html`.

## slot(ctx, id): string and hasSlot(ctx, id): boolean

`hasSlot` uses `Object.hasOwn`. An empty string is provided. A missing slot makes `slot` return `''`.

A function slot is called with the same context. `null` and `undefined` become `''`. A non-string return throws `TypeError` (`slot "<id>" returned <type>, expected a string`). A slot that is not a string or function throws `TypeError` (`slot "<id>" is null|number|..., expected a string or function`). The part that called `slot` is the part recorded on the trace.

## renderMany(jobs, options?): RenderResult[]

Every job shares `TProps`. A job is `{ template, props?, slots? }`. Omitted props become `{}`. `options` is only `{ onError? }`.

`throw` (default) lets the first `RenderError` escape. Later jobs do not run. `collect` returns one result per job, including failures.

This is the batch entry for many templates of one props shape. Different props types are separate batches. Do not add a global registry to work around that.

## defineEmailTemplate(input): Template<EmailProps>

`input` is `{ id, parts? }`. `parts` are custom steps. Built-in order: `head`, `main`, custom parts, `footer`. A custom part whose id is `head`, `main`, `footer`, or `compose` fails validation.

Shell parts call `head`, `main`, and `footer` with only the string props that were actually passed. A slot of the same id replaces that fragment: `slot(ctx, 'head' | 'main' | 'footer')`.

Compose reads rendered keys. Custom ids, in part order, are joined with `\n` and placed after `main` inside the `mainHtml` argument of `document`. With no custom parts, the HTML equals:

```ts
document({
  headHtml: head(props),
  mainHtml: main(props),
  footerHtml: footer(props),
});
```

`content()` is not called. A custom part may call it and return that string.

`renderEmail(template, props = {}, options?)` accepts an `EmailTemplate` input or an already defined `Template<EmailProps>` (`compose` is a function). It returns `RenderResult`.

`EmailProps` (all optional): `title`, `preview`, `heading`, `bodyText`, `ctaLabel`, `ctaUrl`, `companyName`, `unsubscribeUrl`.

## document(props?: DocumentProps): string

`DocumentProps` is `BodyProps` plus `headHtml`.

```ts
document({
  headHtml: head({ title: 'Hi', preview: 'peek' }),
  mainHtml: main({ heading: 'Hi', bodyText: 'Body', ctaLabel: 'Go', ctaUrl: 'https://example.com' }),
  footerHtml: footer({ companyName: 'Acme', unsubscribeUrl: 'https://example.com/u' }),
});
```

Shape:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
{headHtml}
<body>
{mainHtml}
{footerHtml}
</body>
</html>
```

`lang` is fixed to `en`. `document()` with no props is a shell: doctype, html, empty head slot, empty body.

## head(props?: HeadProps): string

| Prop | When omitted |
|---|---|
| `title` | empty `<title></title>` |
| `preview` | empty hidden div |

Always emits `<meta charset="utf-8">`, the viewport meta, `<title>`, and `<div style="display:none;max-height:0;overflow:hidden;">`.

## main(props?: MainProps): string

| Prop | When omitted |
|---|---|
| `heading` | empty `<h1>` |
| `bodyText` | empty `<p>`. May contain inline HTML |
| `ctaLabel` | button omitted unless `ctaUrl` is set too |
| `ctaUrl` | button omitted unless `ctaLabel` is set too |

The button is one `<a>` with inline styles. Either prop alone leaves the anchor out.

## footer(props?: FooterProps): string

| Prop | When omitted |
|---|---|
| `companyName` | empty `<p>` |
| `unsubscribeUrl` | no unsubscribe link |

When `unsubscribeUrl` is set, the link text is `Unsubscribe`.

## body(props?: BodyProps): string

| Prop | When omitted |
|---|---|
| `mainHtml` | empty string inside `<body>` |
| `footerHtml` | empty string inside `<body>` |

## content(props?: ContentProps): string

| Prop | When omitted |
|---|---|
| `content` | empty `<div>` |

`content` is raw HTML placed in the div. Callers insert the result where they want it. `document` does not call `content` or `main` itself.
